correctness.rationale: Open-neighborhood domination requires each gap to be at most five (for unselected vertices) and at least one adjacent gap to be at most two at each selected vertex. Thus the number of long gaps is at most floor(t/2) and the maximum length for t selections is 2t+3 floor(t/2). The exhibited words attain the claimed cardinalities in all seven residues. In particular five selections cover at most sixteen cycle positions, and the word (2,5,2,5,1,2) gives six at n=17. Equality for n=7k forces alternating gaps 2 and 5. Each translate repeats its two residues mod 7 k times, so distinct translates differ by at least k deletions; for k>=2 none are adjacent. At k=1 the distance-two pairs give a 7-cycle. Equality for n=7k+2 forces k gaps of five, k+1 of two, and one short-short junction; its position uniquely marks each translate. An exchange must insert into the gap length 7 created by removing a 2/5 junction, since an unfilled length 7 is impossible. Removing at the 2/2 junction creates length 4; any resulting equality configuration must restore the original 2/2 split. Reversing a 2/5 or 5/2 split is legal exactly at the two boundaries of the short-short junction. In fact take the reference set with vertices 7j for 0<=j<=k and 7j+2 for 0<=j<k: translation by 7 removes 2 and adds 5, so both signed shifts are exchanges. There are at most two by the junction argument, and gcd(7,7k+2)=1 gives a single cycle.

value.rationale: This corrects a concrete published numerical claim for a natural invariant, using a uniform sharp density argument rather than checking one counterexample. It also determines whether local moves can connect optima in two infinite residue classes, identifying the exact cyclic translation step or the absence of all moves. The exchange invariant and the finite obstruction at n=17 are independently useful for reconfiguration and polynomial baselines; no additional significance is assigned to recounting the previously known seven sets.
residual_risks: There is no claim of a full domination polynomial, a reconfiguration classification in all residues, or an extension to higher graph powers.
